# Appeal of Denial — Neck (Cervical) Fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-11**
**Member: Jordan Alvarez | Member ID: W482428991**
**Reference Number: POC-177B09D7A6-51151**
**Governing Policy: Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I)** — https://www.uhcprovider.com/content/dam/provider/docs/public/policies/comm-medical-drug/spinal-fusion-decompression.pdf (effective 2026-04-01)

Dear UnitedHealthcare Appeals Review Team,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my prior authorization request for a cervical (neck) fusion, ACDF, CPT 22551. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I want to walk through what the plan's own policy, Spinal Fusion and Decompression (2026T0639I), says, and compare it to what is actually in my medical records.

The policy states:

> "Coverage Rationale Spinal procedures for the treatment of spine pain are proven and medically necessary in certain circumstances ."

My records show a clear clinical picture supporting that this is one of those circumstances: an MRI of my cervical spine on 2026-06-04 showed a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression. This is paired with a physical exam showing positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to that same imaged level, along with radicular pain, numbness in my right thumb and index finger, and weakness — all on the same side and at the same level shown on the MRI.

The policy also states:

> "Surgery may be an option for individuals whose pain cannot be controlled by more conservative methods (National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, 2023)."

My records document that conservative treatment was tried and did not resolve my symptoms: 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, with 18 visits completed between 2026-05-14 and 2026-07-09; 4 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief; and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. My symptoms have persisted for 24 months and have progressed.

I also want to point out a concern about how the denial was applied. Several of the excerpts in the plan's own policy that appear to be the basis for medical-necessity review — including the language on:

> "A loss of structural support of the spine that leads to abnormal and increased movement between vertebrae outside of normal physiological limits, measured by the difference in translational alignment between lumbar vertebrae greater than or equal to 3 mm between views, as documented by flexion-extension radiographs or comparison of a supine and upright image (NASS, 2021)."

and

> "Lumbar Fusion for Lumbar Spinal Stenosis Alone Lumbar spinal stenosis is a common degenerative condition and a frequent indication for surgical intervention when conservative treatment fails."

— refer specifically to the **lumbar** spine. My procedure is a **cervical** fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6. I have not been shown any cervical-specific imaging criterion that my MRI or exam findings failed to meet. If the plan applied a lumbar-specific measurement (such as the 3 mm translational alignment criterion) to a cervical spine case, or did not identify which specific imaging criterion for cervical fusion was not satisfied, I am asking that this be clarified and corrected.

Similarly, the policy's language on:

> "Dividing treatment of symptomatic, multisite spinal pathology via an anterior or posterior approach into serial or Staged Multiple Sessions when one session can address all sites is unproven and not medically necessary due to insufficient evidence of safety and efficacy."

does not appear to apply to my case, as my records describe a single-level finding (C5-C6) and a single planned procedure, not staged multi-site surgery.

The policy also notes:

> "Medical records documentation may be required to assess whether the member meets the clinical criteria for coverage but does not guarantee coverage of the service requested;"

I understand this means documentation alone does not guarantee approval. That is exactly why I am asking the plan to review the specific imaging and exam findings above against whatever specific imaging criterion for cervical fusion was actually applied to my case — because that specific criterion was not identified in my denial notice.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

I understand from the policy that medical necessity review for this procedure relies in part on InterQual® criteria, which is licensed clinical review software rather than a document I can access on my own. I am asking, in writing, for the plan to provide **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination**. I believe I am entitled to this information under federal ERISA and ACA appeal rules, which require that I be given, free of charge, the specific rule or criterion the plan relied on to deny my claim. Without this information, I am not able to fully understand which imaging finding was considered insufficient.

## What I am asking for

I am asking UnitedHealthcare to reconsider this denial in light of the medical records described above, and to identify the specific cervical-spine imaging criterion that my case did not meet, or to approve the requested cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) based on the documentation already submitted by Dr. Lindqvist.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-07** (180 days from the date of the denial notice, per that notice). I am submitting this appeal by signing in at member.uhc.com and/or by calling the number on my member ID card, and/or by sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Lindqvist's office to complete this review.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Jordan Alvarez
Member ID: W482428991
Date: [date of signing]
Phone: [patient phone number]
Address: [patient mailing address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
